overview: Aegyptosaurus was a titanosaurian sauropod from Cretaceous North Africa. The wiki dataset records it from Egypt and Niger, and PBDB links it to several units including the Baharije Formation and Tegama-related deposits.

Its scientific history is shaped by loss as much as discovery: early North African dinosaur material described by Ernst Stromer was heavily affected by wartime destruction. As a result, Aegyptosaurus remains a useful but incomplete signal of sauropod diversity in northern Africa.

fossilSites.name: Tegama-related deposits
fossilSites.note: PBDB lists Nigerien records from Tegama and associated units.

articles.title: Why it matters
articles.body: Aegyptosaurus helps document African titanosaur distribution before the latest Cretaceous, even though its material is incomplete.

articles.title: Evidence limit
articles.body: Because historical material was lost and the taxon is not represented by abundant complete skeletons, size and anatomy should be treated as approximate.

record.description: Aegyptosaurus baharijensis was a titanosaur from Cenomanian rocks of Egypt. Its name-bearing bones were fragmentary and were destroyed during the Second World War, so much of its diagnosis now depends on Stromer's descriptions and illustrations.
facts: The type series included vertebrae and limb bones, not a complete skeleton.
Material from elsewhere in North Africa has been referred historically, but not all referrals can be demonstrated to belong to the type species.

review.ageReviewNote: The type material came from the Cenomanian Bahariya Formation.

evidence.material: A fragmentary, now-destroyed type series of vertebral and appendicular bones.
evidence.confidenceLimit: No precise body plan or maximum size can be established from the lost fragmentary type.
